from climate_database import query_climate_database
import inspect

def query_climate_database(db_file, country, year_begin, year_end, month):
    # Establish database connection
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_file)

    # SQL query to join tables and filter based on input conditions
    query = f'''
        SELECT 
            stations.NAME, 
            stations.LATITUDE, 
            stations.LONGITUDE, 
            countries.Name AS Country, 
            temperatures.Year, 
            temperatures.Month, 
            temperatures.Temp
        FROM temperatures
        JOIN stations ON temperatures.ID = stations.ID
        JOIN countries ON substr(stations.ID, 1, 2) = countries."FIPS 10-4"
        WHERE countries.Name = "{country}" 
          AND temperatures.Year BETWEEN {year_begin} AND {year_end} 
          AND temperatures.Month = {month}
        ORDER BY stations.NAME, stations.LATITUDE, stations.LONGITUDE, Country, temperatures.Year, temperatures.Month, temperatures.Temp;
    '''
    # Execute query and load results into a Pandas DataFrame
    df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
    
    # Close the database connection
    conn.close()
    
    return df

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import plotly.express as px
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

def temperature_coefficient_plot(db_file, country, year_begin, year_end, month, min_obs, **kwargs):
    """
    Creates interactive map showing the average yearly temperature change for each stations, within given range.
    
    Arguments:
    db_file - source database file
    country - country of stations
    year_begin, year_end - year range of station data
    month - month of observation data
    min_obs - number of minimum data for each station
    
    Returns:
    plotly scatter_mapbox of showing average yearly temperature change of each station
    """
    # Establish database connection
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_file)

    # SQL query to join tables and filter based on input conditions
    query = f'''
        SELECT 
            stations.NAME, 
            stations.LATITUDE, 
            stations.LONGITUDE, 
            countries.Name AS Country, 
            temperatures.Year, 
            temperatures.Month, 
            temperatures.Temp
        FROM temperatures
        JOIN stations ON temperatures.ID = stations.ID
        JOIN countries ON substr(stations.ID, 1, 2) = countries."FIPS 10-4"
        WHERE countries.Name = "{country}" 
          AND temperatures.Year BETWEEN {year_begin} AND {year_end} 
          AND temperatures.Month = {month}
        ORDER BY stations.NAME, stations.LATITUDE, stations.LONGITUDE, Country, temperatures.Year, temperatures.Month, temperatures.Temp;
    '''
    # Execute query and load results into a Pandas DataFrame
    df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
    
    # Close the database connection
    conn.close()
    
    df = df[df.groupby("NAME")["NAME"].transform("count") >= min_obs]

    def compute_slope(group):
        X = group[["Year"]]  # Independent variable (2D)
        y = group["Temp"]     # Dependent variable (1D)

        if len(group) > 1:  # Ensure enough data points for regression
            model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
            return model.coef_[0]  # Extract slope (coefficient)
        else:
            return None  # Not enough data points for regression

    # Compute the coefficient for each station and merge it back into the original DataFrame
    coefficients = df.groupby("NAME").apply(compute_slope).reset_index(name="LR_Coefficient")


    #re-groupby name to have only one value for each stations instead of repeating rows of same stations
    df = df.groupby(["NAME"])[["LATITUDE", "LONGITUDE"]].first()
    
    # Merge the coefficients back into the original DataFrame
    df = df.merge(coefficients, on="NAME", how="left")
    
    
    df["LR_Coefficient"] = df["LR_Coefficient"].round(4)


    fig = px.scatter_mapbox(
        df,
        lat="LATITUDE",
        lon="LONGITUDE",
        color="LR_Coefficient",  # Use LR Coefficient for color scale
        size=[10] * len(df),  # Adjust size to be uniform
        hover_name="NAME",
        hover_data={"LATITUDE": True, "LONGITUDE": True, "LR_Coefficient": True},
        labels={"LR_Coefficient": "Average Yearly Temperature Change"},
        title = f"Average Yearly Temperature Change by Station of {country} from {year_begin} to {year_end} at month of {month}",
        color_continuous_midpoint=0,  # Center color scale at 0

        **kwargs
        
       
    )
        

    # Show figure
    return fig


'''
temperature_coefficient_plot("HW1_database.db", "India", 1980, 2020, 1,
                             min_obs = 1)
'''
color_map = px.colors.diverging.RdGy_r # choose a colormap

fig = temperature_coefficient_plot("HW1_database.db", "India", 1980, 2020, 1, 
                                   min_obs = 10,
                                   zoom = 2,
                                   mapbox_style="carto-positron",
                                   color_continuous_scale=color_map)

fig.show()

                                                



#I want to know the average temperature gap between coldest and hottest temperature, by elevation
#Like, maybe elevation makes the temperature difference over a year more severe?

def tempgap_elevation(db_file, country, year_begin, year_end, min_obs, **kwargs):
    """
    Prints line graph of showing temperature gap within a year versus elevation.
    Motivation was to know the average temperature gap between coldest and hottest temperature, by elevation.
    Maybe elevation makes the temperature difference over a year more severe?
    
    Arguments:
    db_file - source database file
    country - country of stations
    year_begin, year_end - year range of station data
    month - month of observation data
    min_obs - number of minimum data for each station
    
    Returns:
    plotly line graph of showing average temperature gap (within year) by elevation
    
    """
    # Establish database connection
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_file)

    # SQL query to join tables and filter based on input conditions
    query = f'''
        SELECT 
            stations.NAME, 
            stations.LATITUDE, 
            stations.LONGITUDE, 
            stations.STNELEV,
            countries.Name AS Country, 
            temperatures.Year, 
            temperatures.Month, 
            temperatures.Temp
        FROM temperatures
        JOIN stations ON temperatures.ID = stations.ID
        JOIN countries ON substr(stations.ID, 1, 2) = countries."FIPS 10-4"
        WHERE countries.Name = "{country}" 
          AND temperatures.Year BETWEEN {year_begin} AND {year_end} 
        ORDER BY stations.NAME, stations.LATITUDE, stations.LONGITUDE, Country, temperatures.Year, temperatures.Month, temperatures.Temp;
    '''
    # Execute query and load results into a Pandas DataFrame
    df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
    
    # Close the database connection
    conn.close()
    
    df = df[df.groupby("NAME")["NAME"].transform("count") >= min_obs]
    
    # Step 1: Calculate yearly temperature gap (hottest - coldest) for each station
    temp_gap = df.groupby(["NAME", "Year"])["Temp"].agg(lambda x: x.max() - x.min()).reset_index(name="Temp_Gap")

    # Step 2: Compute average temperature gap per station
    avg_temp_gap = temp_gap.groupby("NAME")["Temp_Gap"].mean().reset_index(name="Avg_Temp_Gap")

    # Step 3: Merge with station elevation data
    station_elevation = df.groupby("NAME")["STNELEV"].first().reset_index()
    final_df = avg_temp_gap.merge(station_elevation, on="NAME")
    

    # Step 4: Create line plot (Elevation vs. Avg Temp Gap)
    fig = px.line(
        final_df.sort_values("STNELEV"),  # Sort by elevation for better visualization
        x="STNELEV",
        y="Avg_Temp_Gap",
        markers=True,  # Show points along the line
        title="Average Temperature Gap vs. Station Elevation",
        labels={"STNELEV": "Station Elevation (m)", "Avg_Temp_Gap": "Avg Temp Gap (°C)"},
        **kwargs  # Pass additional arguments dynamically
    )

    return fig


color_map = px.colors.diverging.RdGy_r # choose a colormap

fig = tempgap_elevation("HW1_database.db", "India", 1980, 2020, 
                                   min_obs = 10)

fig.show()

#maybe create heatmap showing, by latitude (or region), how severe is the avg_temp has changed over years?

from climate_database import query_temp_in_longitude

def gbw_by_lat(db_file, year_begin, year_end, longitude_begin, longitude_end, month, **kwargs):
    """
    Accepts specified year range and longitude range
    Returns plotly density_mapbox of showing average temperature change by latitude
    
    Arguments:
    db_file - source database file
    country - country of stations
    year_begin, year_end - year range of station data
    longitude_begin, longitude_end - longitude range of station data
    month - month of observation data
    
    Returns:
    plotly density_mapbox of showing average temperature change by latitude
    
    
    
    """
    
    df = query_temp_in_longitude(db_file, year_begin, year_end, longitude_begin, longitude_end, month)

    
    def compute_slope(group):
        X = group[["Year"]]  # Independent variable (2D)
        y = group["Temp"]     # Dependent variable (1D)

        if len(group) > 1:  # Ensure enough data points for regression
            model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
            return model.coef_[0]  # Extract slope (coefficient)
        else:
            return None  # Not enough data points for regression

    # Compute the coefficient for each station and merge it back into the original DataFrame
    coefficients = df.groupby("NAME").apply(compute_slope).reset_index(name="LR_Coefficient")


    # re-groupby name to have only one value for each stations instead of repeating rows of same stations
    df = df.groupby(["NAME"])[["LATITUDE", "LONGITUDE"]].first()
    
    # Merge the coefficients back into the original DataFrame
    df = df.merge(coefficients, on="NAME", how="left")
    
    #return df
    
    
    # Add column of latitude bins of 3-degree intervals for every row
    df["Latitude_Bin"] = pd.cut(df["LATITUDE"], bins=range(-90, 90, 3), right=False)
    
    # Group by latitude bins and calculate average temperature
    avg_tempInc_by_lat = df.groupby("Latitude_Bin")["LR_Coefficient"].mean().reset_index()
    avg_tempInc_by_lat["LR_Coefficient"] = avg_tempInc_by_lat["LR_Coefficient"].round(4)

    
    # Compute midpoint of each latitude bin (for visualization)
    avg_tempInc_by_lat["Latitude_Mid"] = avg_tempInc_by_lat["Latitude_Bin"].apply(lambda x: (x.left + x.right) / 2)
    avg_tempInc_by_lat['Latitude_Mid'] = pd.to_numeric(avg_tempInc_by_lat['Latitude_Mid'], errors='coerce')
    
    avg_tempInc_by_lat = avg_tempInc_by_lat.dropna() #drop rows with NaN to avoid error with mapbox
    
    # Want difference by latitude, so data should be uniform over longitudes
    # To show that in mapbox, create just one middle longitude for displaying purpose and assign it to every row
    avg_tempInc_by_lat["Longitude_Mid"] = (longitude_begin + longitude_end) / 2
    
    avg_tempInc_by_lat['Latitude_Bin'] = avg_tempInc_by_lat['Latitude_Bin'].astype(str)  # Convert category to string for displaying in mapbox

    # debugging purpose
    #print(avg_tempInc_by_lat.dtypes)
    #return avg_tempInc_by_lat
    

    fig = px.density_mapbox(
        avg_tempInc_by_lat,
        lat="Latitude_Mid",
        lon= "Longitude_Mid",
        z="LR_Coefficient",  # Temperature data determines heat intensity
        radius=20,  # Adjusts heatmap radius
        hover_name="Latitude_Bin",
        hover_data={"Latitude_Bin": True, "LR_Coefficient": True},
        color_continuous_scale="Jet",  # Temperature-based color gradient
        title="Temperature Change (Global Warming) Heatmap of Stations",
        labels={"LR_Coefficient": "Average Yearly Temperature Change"},
        mapbox_style="carto-positron",
        zoom=0,
        **kwargs  # Pass additional arguments dynamically
    )
    
    # Restrict map boundaries to specific longitude & latitude range
    fig.update_layout(
        mapbox_bounds={"west": longitude_begin, "east": longitude_end},
        width=800,  # Increase map width
        height=800   # Increase map height
    )


    return fig


gbw_by_lat("HW1_database.db", 1980, 2020, 80, 90, 6).show()

This shows the overall information about dataset. We can create various visualization, but I will show how to make visualization for discrete data vs numerical data. For instance, I will create a box plot of culmen length by each species, to compare how long each species’ culmen length is.
We would need to use two most useful visualization packages: seaborn and matplotlib.

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

#For readability, I put line change in the middle of species name.
penguins['Species'] = penguins['Species'].str.replace(' (', '\n(') 

#Creating box plot using seaborn boxplot
#Since we are differentiating data by species, set 'Species' for data in x line
#Since we want to know culmen length of each species, set 'Culmen length' for data in y line
sns.boxplot(x='Species', y='Culmen Length (mm)', data=penguins)

#Put appropriate title of plot using matplotlib command
plt.title('Box Plot of Culmen Length by Species')
plt.show()








The plot shows the distribution and average of culmen length of each speices. From this, we can see that Chinstrap Penguin has longest culmen length overall, and they have around 5 mm of error margin (from 25th percentile to 75th percentile).
With seaborn and matplotlib, it is very easy to visualize dataframe.
